overall_summary: Analysis of the recent data reveals that extreme cosmic scenarios, planetary physics ('What If' and bizarre weather on exoplanets), and high-contrast space anomalies are driving the highest views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes-per-view). Specifically, videos featuring hypothetical planetary destruction, extreme weather conditions on alien worlds (diamonds, liquid metal, dark matter planets), and timeline/physics anomalies are outperforming traditional static factoids by a wide margin. Engagement spikes notably on content that combines speculative danger ('What If You Fell Into...') with exotic space environments.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Planetary Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) show exceptional views-per-day and like rates relative to older, static format facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes 'What If' planetary survival scenarios blending physics and exotic materials.

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre Alien Weather / Exotic Planet Phenomena
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing extreme atmospheric conditions such as 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,031 views, 36 likes) demonstrate strong immediate hook retention.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form deep dives into extreme, counter-intuitive exoplanet physics and meteorological anomalies.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics centered around mild psychological tricks or memory facts like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' generated very low traction (5 to 53 views, 0 likes across multiple re-runs).
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychology micro-facts unless framed through an extreme, high-conflict neurological survival or mystery angle.

weak_patterns.evidence: Simple biological trivia such as 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (when not paired with aggressive hooks or narrative tension) plateau quickly compared to space/physics content.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content strictly toward cinematic survival, horror-tinged micro-stories, or extreme evolutionary anomalies rather than basic trivia.

next_video.concept: What Happens If You Fall Into the Coldest Known Object in the Universe (The Boomerang Nebula)
next_video.opening_direction: Start inside absolute zero, demonstrating instantly how human breath freezes and shatters in a fraction of a second.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that this nebula is actually colder than the background radiation of space itself, sucking thermal energy out of anything that enters it faster than liquid nitrogen.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performing 'What If' and extreme temperature/space mechanics niche that yields top-tier views and like rates.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must focus specifically on the Boomerang Nebula, avoiding previously used planets or stars like TrES-2b or Venus.
Must not reuse phrasing from past titles.
Strictly factual astrophysical description without fictional framing.
